I am a woman of 43 years, farming here in the North East. My husband and I own this land, and maize is what feeds my children. I will buy some urea and NPK from the market if the price is not too high this year, but I cannot afford much — the rains have been uncertain and last year I lost some of my harvest to the army worm, so I must spend small money on chemical to spray. I keep some goats and chickens, so I carry their droppings to the field before the rains. I use the seed I saved from last harvest because improved seed from the agro-dealer is expensive and not always available in my village. My children and I will do most of the work, but at planting and weeding time I will call two or three people from the village to help me for a few days.
